page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.4xlarge is a compute-focused instance powered by the KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 16 threads, running on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI. Memory capacity is allocated at 16.0 GB, yielding a compact 1:1 ratio of 1.0 GB RAM per vCPU. The instance comes without bundled local storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier multi-threaded processing alongside modest single-core throughput. The instance achieves a multi-core Geekbench score of 6,191.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 12,997.09, reflecting average multi-core efficiency in parallel tasks such as Clang compilation (10,481.0) and ray tracing (10,435.0). In contrast, single-core metrics fall within the lower quartile, highlighted by a single-core Geekbench score of 991.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 19.22 GB/sec. Large uncached memory operations register 74.68 GB/sec for sequential reads and 43.33 GB/sec for writes.

The 1:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation creates a distinct operational tradeoff. While cost-efficient for parallel tasks that do not consume large memory footprints per thread, it restricts deployments of large data processing frameworks, large in-memory caches, or heavy memory-bound machine learning pipelines, as shown by weak performance during 7B model LLM inference. Static web serving reaches 9.78 GB/sec and Redis SET operations hit 11.38 million operations per second.

The ecs.ic5.4xlarge server is best suited for horizontally scaled computing environments, continuous integration build workers, CPU-driven batch encoding, microservices, and web servers with external storage backends.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor at 2.5 GHz, supported by 16.0 GB of memory and a 5 Gbps network interface, without integrated local storage. With an exact 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the hardware configuration targets compute density rather than memory-heavy footprints. Benchmark evaluations place multi-threaded capabilities within average cloud parameters, recording 12,997.09 in PassMark CPU and 6,191.0 in multi-core Geekbench, whereas single-core benchmarks place in the lower quartile. Memory throughput achieves 74.68 GB/sec on large uncached reads. The server is practical for parallelized build environments, batch processing workloads, and distributed stateless microservices.
